name: audit
body:
Confirmed a smaller reproducer on the current cargo-audit 0.23.0 Linux binary (2026-11-14):

```toml
version = 4
[[package]]
name = "audit-panic-repro"
version = "0.1.0"
dependencies = ["missing 1.0.0"]
```

Save as bad.lock and run `cargo audit --file bad.lock --deny warnings`. It exits 101 and panics at `cargo-audit/src/presenter.rs:160:14`: `invalid Cargo.lock dependency tree: Resolution("failed to find dependency: missing 1.0.0")`.

An inconsistent lockfile should fail, but with a normal diagnostic rather than a presenter panic. Our real failure also contained duplicate syn entries and a reference to an absent syn version. Local workaround: regenerate the lock with Cargo and run `cargo metadata --locked --format-version 1` before auditing. Suggested change: propagate dependency-tree resolution errors from the presenter instead of expecting success, and add the four-line fixture as a regression.

Consumer evidence and fixture: https://github.com/link-foundation/rust-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/pull/248 .

name: artifact
body:
Current consumer verification for v8.0.2 (`9000827ccba6bdab643e8b6fd33ac0654aef8333`): this extraction-chain workaround is still necessary in https://github.com/link-foundation/rust-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/pull/248 .

Minimal workflow remains a normal artifact download with `NODE_OPTIONS: --throw-deprecation`; the vendored MatcherStream/Buffer reproducer in the earlier comment isolates DEP0005 without credentials. Our composite retains `skip-decompress: true`, SHA-256 mismatch failure, and validated Python ZIP extraction. Its regression suite covers traversal, symlinks, corrupt archives, merging and actual artifact round trips.

Suggested upstream fix remains replacing the obsolete ZIP/Buffer code and rebuilding the shipped bundle; test real extraction with deprecations fatal. Existing PR #490 is still open. We keep this report linked rather than open a duplicate.

name: pages
body:
Verified against the current v5.0.1 bundle on 2026-11-14: `dist/index.js` still contains `module.exports = require("punycode")` (module 85477). This remains distinct from retired Node runtime warnings.

Minimal reproduction: a normal `actions/deploy-pages@v5` step for a valid Pages artifact; alternatively `node --throw-deprecation -e 'require("punycode")'` demonstrates the bundled core import's failure mode. Consumer: https://github.com/link-foundation/rust-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/pull/248 .

The temporary consumer workaround suppresses only DEP0040 for this action; all other warnings and deployment errors remain visible. Updating the dependency importing core punycode to its userland replacement, regenerating dist, and running a deployment smoke test with deprecations fatal would remove this exception. We have no evidence connecting this warning to the 404 reported in another comment.

name: actionlint
body:
Reconfirmed on Linux with the current 1.7.12 release while updating https://github.com/link-foundation/rust-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/pull/248 .

The existing minimal workflow with `concurrency: {group: release, queue: max}` still produces `unexpected key "queue" for "concurrency" section`. Our release workflows require queue serialization and retain only the existing narrow ignore for this diagnostic; all other Actionlint, ShellCheck and workflow security checks remain active.

The proposed enum/schema validation in #654 would remove the local exception. No new issue is needed; this adds another current-release consumer and verification result to the existing reproducer.

name: lychee
body:
Current downstream confirmation: the latest release endpoint still returns lychee 0.24.2 (2026-11-14). We retain a bounded external retry adapter in https://github.com/link-foundation/rust-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/pull/248 for this reported connect-reset gap.

The minimal HTTPS RST server in this issue remains the relevant reproduction. Our offline regression tests preserve failure for permanent 404 responses, bound retries for unanswered connections and transient 429/5xx statuses, and reuse the same accepted statuses and user agent. Increasing lychee's retry count alone cannot change the connect-phase classifier.

The existing proposed fix that examines connect-phase I/O errors and unwraps nested `io::Error` values would let us remove the adapter once released. This records the consumer workaround rather than duplicate the report.

name: buildx
body:
Verified v4.4.1 includes #609: `Docker.pull(image)` now runs before creating the builder, with bounded transient retries in actions-toolkit. We removed our duplicate pre-pull/backoff implementation in https://github.com/link-foundation/rust-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/pull/248 .

One remaining feature gap is independent registry fallback. Reproduction: canonical Docker Hub is unreachable while `mirror.gcr.io/moby/buildkit:v0.35.0` is available. Retagging a mirror image locally no longer avoids the action's unconditional canonical pre-pull. Our small adapter tries the official action against the canonical image, then invokes it against the mirror image only on failure; failure of both sources stays fatal. Offline mocked-action tests cover both recovery and disabled/exhausted fallback.

Suggested optional feature: accept ordered bootstrap-image mirror references and apply the existing upstream retry classifier to each, before creating a builder. This is a mirror feature, separate from the generic workflow retries discussed above.

name: codeql
body:
Additional current-bundle case from https://github.com/link-foundation/rust-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/actions/runs/43556886733 (CodeQL bundle 2.27.4): three `serde_json::json!` test fixtures in a standalone rust-script are reported as unexpanded macros. Source: `scripts/check-cargo-lock.rs` at main revision `7b819f8a40b9a2261792aabed7d055d146d8fe1e`.

Minimal shape is a standalone .rs file with rust-script inline Cargo metadata declaring serde_json, plus `let value = serde_json::json!({"packages": []});`. Rust-script compiles the tests, but extraction reports missing macro expansion. We cannot yet establish whether inline-manifest discovery or another extractor limitation is the cause.

Local workaround: parse equivalent literal JSON with `serde_json::from_str::<Value>(...).unwrap()`; retain all acceptance assertions and keep our SARIF extraction-warning gate fatal. Suggested upstream investigation: discover standalone inline Cargo dependencies during extraction and add this fixture to macro-expansion coverage. PR with before/after fixture and original logs: https://github.com/link-foundation/rust-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/pull/248 .
